manual link creation is di cult, expensive and inconsistent.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the construction and retrieval of hypertext, but with a particular interest in the role of the human indexer and in the e ects of the quality of the hypertext on the e ectiveness and cost of information retrieval.
the e ectiveness and e ciency of manual hypertext link construction, and with the development of methods for its improvement.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, whilst the creation of links by humans is a necessary component of hypertext systems, it is not a sufficient one.

, whilst the creation of hypertext documents by manual means is generally preferred to automatic methods, the quality of such documents is likely to be su ering from a lack of consistency amongst the human link creators.

manual methods of link construction are not generally superior to automatic methods, and that the latter are in any case necessary in order to provide the consistency and coverage required to support e ective information retrieval in hypertext.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the quality of manual link creation is variable, the quality of automatic link creation is not; and that, in the absence of any compelling reason to the contrary, the use of automatic methods is to be preferred.
manual methods of link creation can be very e ective, but that the e ects of inconsistency amongst manual link-creators can be very signi cant.

manual and automatic link creation are complementary, and that the two approaches should be considered together in the construction of hypertext systems, and that the results of this comparison should be made available to the users of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consistency of human link-creaters is low and highly variable.
, while manual link construction can be expected to produce hypertexts of high quality, the quality of these hypertexts is not guaranteed.
the creation of hypertext documents by manual means is an activity that requires careful consideration of the quality of the resulting hypertexts.
